pg:https://www.avclub.com/game-theory-gr.desc: Grand Theft Auto VI and The Game Awards deserve each other
paras: The current reason I’m feeling like a frog slow-boiling in the warm waters of a fictitious, it-took-human-beings-10-million-hours-of-computer-drudgery-to-model Florida city, though, is that other tentpole event sticking out of end of the annual gaming calendar, like a piece of rebar lodged in Phineas Gage’s head: The Game Awards. After all, it was Tuesday morning when Geoff Keighley’s celebration of video game commercials (with the occasional trophy, or dollop of supposed activism, thrown in) announced that GTA VI had been nominated for Game Of The Year, despite, again, the total number of people who’d played it at that point likely not breaking a thousand.

I’m not suggesting any kind of impropriety here, mind you; the critics who voted for the game’s nomination are probably from the major outlets that have played it—and even if they weren’t, I’m open to the idea that Grand Theft Auto VI should have a GOTY nomination locked down from this particular body, basically by default. Because, honestly, GTA and The Game Awards deserve each other.

You can argue, as I imagine Keighley would, that this kind of communal interest is a net benefit to gaming, creating a force of attention so large that not even our collective cultural gatekeepers can deny it. (Because, god, but is there nothing that a certain kind of gaming brain can’t stand then to be casually dismissed by The New York Times.) Meanwhile, those of us on the skeptic side can point to all the ways the TGAs do what monocultures always do, i.e., grind down massive amounts of diversity and varied experiences into a uniform nubbin while extracting as much cash from folks as humanly possible.

pg:https://www.vaticannews.va/en/world/n.desc: The United Nations climate summit, COP31, has been meeting in Türkiye, with reliance on fossil fuels, the electricity grid, and concerns about ...
paras: The global energy transition has been one of the main topics at the UN climate summit, COP31, in Türkiye, where countries have been discussing how to move away from fossil fuels and how to overcome the financial and structural obstacles in the way.

The problem looks different depending on the country. Oil and gas producers must prepare for falling revenues and find new sources of income, while fuel-importing nations want alternatives that would leave them less exposed to volatile energy markets. Both face the difficult task of securing the investment, infrastructure and international backing the transition requires.
Türkiye, the summit host, has set its own goal: to raise the share of global energy consumption met by electricity from non-fossil sources from just over 20% today to 35% by 2035.

pg:https://www.theguardian.com/film/2026.desc: Was it all a dream? Has Bond been in hiding? Or will Robert Pattinson simply report to HR on his first day? Russell T Davies, David Hare and more give their takes
paras: Colin Vaines, producer of Coriolanus and Film Stars Don’t Die in Liverpool, says the superhero-type reboot is the most probable way forward. “It’s possible that, like Holmes, he could turn up having escaped death and then hidden out to protect his friends from assaults on them by the villains. But I believe it’s way more likely that they are starting again as though nothing has happened, like it’s a multiverse in a Marvel movie where old or dead or alternate versions of superheroes just turn up and do their thing.”

Questions had been asked before over the future of the Bond character, particularly after it was revealed in the run-up to No Time to Die in 2019 that the 007 codename was to be given to Lashana Lynch’s new MI6 agent Nomi. Was Bond really about to be put out to pasture? The ambiguity of the future of Bond – which was seen by some as a new front in the culture war – was underscored by Craig’s open dislike of the role, and his determination that No Time to Die was his last film in the role.

Vaines suggests that the Bond death narrative was Craig’s way of making sure he never had to come back to a series that, at that time, was still under the control of its original production company Eon. “I believe Daniel Craig wanted a definitive line drawn under his Bond, which everyone agreed on at the time. The Eon team may well have just planned to effectively start again the way that rather good opening sequence in the first Craig Bond played out, establishing after two kills that he was an 00 agent. That always felt like a excellent origin story.”

Levent Alpöge, a Turkish American mathematician, on Friday posted a note on his personal website saying that Claude, the AI software, had helped prove the Riemann hypothesis. He says that Claude helped develop a solution to the problem during the course of about six weeks.

paras: New Delhi: Negotiations at the UN climate summit in Turkey extended into “extra time” on Saturday, as consensus on the outcome document remained elusive amid deep divisions among nations over how the text should address fossil fuel emissions in an increasingly warming world, while also taking into account the Global South’s demand for economic growth.

From the outset of the 31st Conference of the Parties (COP31) to the UN Framework Convention on Climate Change, references to fossil fuels remained central to the deadlock, pushing the summit into overtime.

pg:https://theconversation.com/cop31-why.desc: Negotiations broke down over whether to directly address fossil fuels, leaving the most climate-vulnerable nations deeply disappointed.
paras: The UN’s annual two-week climate summit, Cop31, has ended in failure. Countries could not find consensus on a final agreement. It is the first such failure in more than 20 years.

The summit started relatively smoothly. In fact, the conference agenda was adopted within a few hours on day one, as country parties found nothing objectionable. At the time, this event looked like it might be smooth sailing: another summit simply focused on implementing policies agreed in previous years.

But week two became explosive. First, the draft agreement – which if adopted would have been known as the Antalya Accords – conceded that we have failed to keep global temperature rise below 1.5˚C and that the world is entering a period of “overshoot”. pg:https://time.com/article/2026/11/23/c.desc: Don't confuse the lack of another global accord with the lack of international engagement to tackle climate change.
paras: Participants sleep under COP31 signage in the main hall on the final day of the COP31 UNFCCC Climate Conference on Nov. 20 in Antalya, Turkey.

In the eleven years since the Paris Agreement, countries around the world have met annually to plot out the global consensus on how to tackle climate change. In some years negotiations led to big breakthroughs. In others, talks simply kept the ball in play, signaling to the world that nations were aligned in their desire to tackle climate change, even if it’s hard to agree on the exact path forward.

So it was a striking moment in the three-decade arc of United Nations climate negotiations when talks fell apart in Turkey over the weekend at this year’s COP31. The decade-long global consensus about the urgency of tackling climate change that produced the Paris Agreement at COP21 in 2015, it seems, came to an end on Sunday. The issues at play were many, of various levels of complexity, but the biggest was rather simple: a group of countries led by Saudi Arabia and Russia resisted reference to phasing out fossil fuels in the final text, and a bloc of 130 countries including the European Union refused to sign on without it.

pg:https://defector.com/oh-no-i-cant-sto.desc: I did not imagine that the release of Grand Theft Auto VI would have any meaningful impact on my life, for the simple reason that I am not a gamer. paras: Add Defector to Google 131CommentsI did not imagine that the release of Grand Theft Auto VI would have any meaningful impact on my life, for the simple reason that I am not a gamer. I know and even respect a few people for whom video games are important, but I mainly regard this in the same way I do friends who really like square dancing, or go to church: nice for them, but not really my business.

While I have, in the past, dated gamers and even come to occasionally enjoy watching them play video games, that was mainly because I'm bossy and liked telling them Go over there, or Open that box, I bet there's something inside. Backseat driving a video game can be fun, but only insofar as I can manipulate what's happening. The appeal of Twitch, where you are simply one of dozens or hundreds of spectators watching someone else play a game, has always been totally, utterly alien to me. This would be true even without the dangers of encountering slurs in a chat or being confronted by the ever-present sight of anything that could be reasonably called "a gaming rig." No thank you.

And yet, I have found my conviction wavering recently as I find myself strangely compelled to click on clip after clip of people playing GTA VI. It started innocently enough, as people kept insisting that this game was teaching men to be thoughtful partners. I watched clips of people doing things Lucia will appreciate: buying groceries, taking her shopping, picking up flowers. I watched a guy make thoughtful decisions about how she might like to wear her hair. Soon I'd moved on to following along as people make Jason lovingly turn their house into a home, or invite Lucia to take the driver's seat on an aquatic adventure.

pg:https://www.dw.com/en/cop-deadlock-pr.desc: COP31 has been branded a failure after countries couldn't reach a final agreement, divided over a reference to "fossil fuels." But was the decision to walk away from a watered-down text actually a show of strength?
paras: After two days of extended talks, representatives from country after country, tiredness etched into each face, voiced their opposition to the so-called "Antalya Pact."

One of the main sticking points: the words "fossil fuels." While some nations, including petrostates like Saudi Arabia and Russia, wanted them omitted from the text, others saw it as a "step backwards" not to include them.

pg:https://www.courthousenews.com/un-cli.desc: It hasn't happened since 2009: International talks to fight climate change ended without any new pledges and commitments.
paras: It hasn't happened since 2009: International talks to fight climate change ended without any new pledges and commitments.

The summit, held this year in Antalya, Turkey, and known as COP31, was overshadowed by geopolitical tensions and wars, the withdrawal of U.S. President Donald Trump from the United Nations process to tackle climate change and growing alarm over the accelerating pace of global warming.

On Sunday, with the faltering talks already in overtime, the EU delegation walked out of the negotiations and said it could not accept a final declaration that did include language over the need to transition away from fossil fuels. The United Kingdom and many developing nations also rejected the proposed text as unacceptable.

pg:https://www.aljazeera.com/opinions/20.desc: The failure exposes a diplomacy that protects fossil-fuel power while leaving vulnerable countries to pay the price.
paras: COP31 ended without an overarching agreement on Sunday in Antalya, Turkiye, after nearly 200 countries failed to agree on a final climate pact. The proposed text could not even name the principal cause of global warming: fossil fuels. The European Union, several Pacific island states and other governments rejected it, while oil-producing countries resisted stronger language. After three decades of annual summits, this was the first such breakdown since 2009.

It is tempting to call this an extraordinary diplomatic failure. But the collapse reveals something more enduring. Climate negotiations have become remarkably effective at keeping governments at the table while avoiding the economic changes that meaningful climate action requires. The system is not designed literally to produce no agreements; it is designed to accommodate interests powerful enough to prevent decisive ones.

Consider what happened in Antalya. The EU objected that the final draft did not even mention fossil fuels. Yet the omission was not a clerical oversight. Earlier language on moving away from oil, gas and coal had been weakened as negotiations proceeded. The summit could not agree on how to implement the agreement reached at COP28 in Dubai in 2023 to transition away from fossil fuels in energy systems. What should have been the starting point for action became the point at which diplomacy broke down.

In the outer solar system, icy bodies are spread widely beyond Neptune. Many are concentrated in the Kuiper Belt, about 38–50 astronomical units (AU; 1 AU is the average Earth–Sun distance of about 150 million km) from the Sun. The problem is that over the past two decades, objects with highly elongated or steeply inclined orbits have been discovered much farther out. It has been pointed out that the gravity of known planets, including Neptune, alone cannot easily explain their movements.

A representative case is Sedna. This body travels around the Sun on a long, elliptical orbit and stays far beyond Neptune's orbit even at its closest approach to the Sun. The gravity of known planets alone cannot easily explain how such an orbit formed. An alternative hypothesis to explain this is "Planet Nine," a hidden giant planet with 5–10 times Earth's mass.

paras: It was a day-and-a-half past the official deadline when the UN climate summit COP31 began to unravel in earnest.

On Sunday morning, the corridors inside the huge expo-style venue in the Turkish city of Antalya were almost empty. Tired groups of delegates and media sat propped against the walls waiting for updates, charging their phones and drinking coffee. Many had barely slept. Australian Energy Minister Chris Bowen – who headed up the COP31 negotiations – reportedly slept for only a few minutes on the final night, as delegates kept waking him.
The talks dragged well into overtime to become the longest summit on record. But it would not finish the way co-presidents Bowen and Turkish Environment Minister Murat Kurum had hoped.

ANTALYA, Turkey – International climate talks in Antalya, Turkey, broke down in overtime hours with a disagreement over how to address fossil fuels, the main cause of global warming.

pg:https://www.pbs.org/newshour/world/th.desc: While negotiations collapsed over one main point of contention — whether to include language about fossil fuels, the main driver of global warming — this fight over this has been building for many years.
paras: NEW YORK (AP) — Going into this year's U.N. climate talks in Turkey, expectations were notably low. But the outcome on Sunday was even worse than expected — a failure to reach an overall agreement on fighting climate change at a time of frequent extreme weather events fueled by rising temperatures.

Gaining traction at this year's summit, known as COP31, was always going to be difficult. Leaders and everyday people alike have plenty to contend with in addition to extreme weather, from wars to shaky economies to fears about artificial intelligence. Last year's climate conference in Brazil, which had all the ingredients for an historic outcome, turned out to be a flop. And for the second year in a row, the United States, the world's richest country and historically No. 1 polluter, did not take part; the Trump administration has pulled the U.S. from climate negotiations.

Still, there was hope, among lifetime environmental campaigners, climate scientists and negotiators from many countries, that there would be some progress on confronting the main cause of climate change: coal, oil and gas.

paras: COP31 started with a sputter and ended in a puff of smoke as almost 200 countries failed to overcome divisions and reach a new deal on how to tackle climate change.
The conference was meant to conclude on Friday, but it ran well into the weekend as impasses over fossil fuels and finance turned COP31 into the longest climate conference ever.

The Antalya pact, drafted by the Turkish and Australian joint presidencies and the deal countries would have accepted had consensus been reached, called on countries to minimise the 1.5°C overshoot, which scientific reports have found is inevitable. The pact also called on developed countries (the EU, UK), historically responsible for higher emissions fuelling the climate crisis, to provide fair finance to developing nations to help them adapt to the impacts of climate change. The pact also invited countries to electrify their economies.

pg:https://www.thecut.com/article/jensen.desc: For his return to Nvidia, Huang ditched his signature black leather in favor of navy cotton.
paras: If you can get past how wild it is that Huang’s Nvidia employees are acting like he just returned from war (he was gone for 11 days), you’ll notice that his jacket appears to be cotton. Clearly, Huang thought that the working man’s fabric would look best as he held his hand to his heart and expressed his gratitude. Black leather would be too flashy for the occasion, but navy cotton? That has just the right amount of humility. That’s a jacket that says, “I’m listening and learning.”

Huang’s “man of the people” jacket looks a lot like one he wore in June during a trip to Seoul. Perhaps he was hoping to show how down to earth he can be by shopping his own closet? Photos from the trip give us a clearer image of the chest logo, which is, of course, Dior. pg:https://gizmodo.com/grand-theft-auto-.desc: Finding it only took three days of grinding.
paras: Given that half the world has been playing Grand Theft Auto VI since its release last Thursday, it’s no surprise that the game’s secrets and Easter eggs are being cracked in record time. Perhaps the most impressive discovery so far is a secret cracked by a player named Memeio, who tweeted that he had spent three days going further and further down a rabbit hole that led him to a portal into… Grand Theft Auto Vice City, circa 2002.

The discovery is another entry in the rich tradition of secrets that return players to earlier entries in a given series. My personal favorite is the various secret levels in the 2016 reboot of Doom, which allowed players to revisit levels from the original 1993 Doom, complete with original graphics, music and sound effects. The GTA VI secret does something similar, but—befitting a game with a 10-figure budget—it takes the idea a step further, also bringing back one of the voice actors from the 2002 game.

The GTA VI secret is hidden behind an awfully convoluted multi-faceted puzzle involving the game’s power stations. Memeio’s video catalogs the sequence of steps needed to solve that puzzle, and… well, you can see why it took him three days of grinding to figure it out.

pg:https://www.cnn.com/2026/11/22/climat.desc: The COP31 climate conference in Antalya, Turkey, collapsed Sunday as countries failed to agree to an overarching deal.
paras: The annual UN climate talks, which stretched deep into overtime over the weekend, hold the dubious honor of being the longest COP in history and the first major breakdown since COP15 in Copenhagen in 2009.

Experts criticized the conference as a stunning failure of leadership at a time when the climate crisis is accelerating with increasingly deadly consequences. “This has been the worst ever COP and its collapse needs to be a wake up call for the world,” said Mohamed Adow, director of the energy think tank Power Shift Africa.

pg:https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/ar.desc: Manchester United and Mauricio Pochettino are furious at how Leny Yoro's red card has been handled by VAR John Brooks and referees' chief Howard Webb
paras: Manchester United reporter in LisbonPublished24 November 2026Manchester United head coach Mauricio Pochettino has questioned the competence of video assistant referee officials after defender Leny Yoro had his red card overturned by the Football Association.
Yoro was sent off eight minutes into United's 4-0 defeat at Liverpool on Sunday after bringing down Aleksander Isak just outside the United penalty area.

United sources say they have conclusive proof it was impossible for Isak to reach the ball after he took a heavy touch, that it would have run on to goalkeeper Senne Lammens and Yoro should not have been punished for denying a goalscoring opportunity.

pg:https://www.cbsnews.com/news/nvidia-j.desc: Attorney General Todd Blanche did not say whether federal investigators interviewed Jensen Huang — who was rehired as CEO on Monday — or examined his relationship with an alleged Chinese spy.
paras: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang still holds a security clearance, multiple sources familiar with the matter told CBS News.

Huang has drawn weeks of scrutiny, following reports that he had an affair with a businesswoman and alleged Chinese intelligence asset whose company is suspected of transferring advanced Nvidia chips to China. Huang resigned as Nvidia's chief executive two weeks ago, but the company's board reinstated him on Monday following direct appeals from President Trump, who said he offered the board an "assurance" that Huang did not pose a national security threat.

Huang never received a defensive security briefing from the administration after he was alerted about businesswoman Alice Huang's alleged ties to China, a source directly familiar with the matter said. Such briefings, also called counterintelligence briefings, help people with a U.S. government security clearance recognize threats.

pg:https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/1.desc: Twenty hostages were released from a supermarket surrounded by police and troops, the president says.
paras: Colombia’s president has said all 20 people held hostage by armed men in a supermarket in the city of Cartagena have been rescued. Security forces stormed the supermarket early on Wednesday, ending a daylong siege.
The hostage incident came after an unsuccessful attempt to rob an armoured vehicle, the Colombian police said.
De la Espriella said the robbers sought refuge in a nearby store after security camera operators alerted police to the attempted robbery.

pg:https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/1.desc: UN allocates $2m for immunisation and medical equipment as Cuban healthcare struggles with critical shortages.
paras: World Health ‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌Organization chief Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus has called for the lifting of a US fuel blockade on Cuba, as shortages dent the island’s once vaunted healthcare system.
Tedros warned that the sanctions were endangering the lives of children on Tuesday, during a ⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠visit to Cuba that included tours of several healthcare facilities in Havana.

During his three-day visit, the United Nations health agency’s top official said his organisation would contribute $2m to help strengthen Cuba’s ‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌national immunisation programme and provide essential medical equipment to healthcare facilities.

pg:https://www.theguardian.com/world/202.desc: WHO chief says life expectancy has fallen from 78.8 years in 2020 to 74.4 in 2025, figures that predate US fuel blockade
paras: WHO chief says life expectancy has fallen from 78.8 years in 2020 to 74.4 in 2025, figures that predate US fuel blockade
Life expectancy has fallen for the first time in Cuba since 1950 as the island reels from a severe economic crisis, the head of the World Health Organization (WHO) said on Tuesday.
On a visit to Havana, WHO chief Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus said life expectancy had fallen from 78.8 years in 2020 to 74.4 years in 2025, the first decline since records began in 1950.

pg:https://www.aljazeera.com/video/newsf.desc: A group of armed men is holding around 20 people hostage in Cartagena, Colombia.
paras: A group of armed men is holding around 20 people hostage in Cartagena, Colombia. The gunmen hid in a supermarket after a failed robbery and are reportedly demanding nearly $2 million to release the hostages.

paras: Former England winger Raheem Sterling has been ⁠spared ⁠an immediate jail sentence after he admitted dangerous driving by inhaling “laughing ⁠gas” while behind the wheel before crashing his Lamborghini.

Sterling, 31, was reported ⁠driving erratically on the M25 and M3 motorways in southern England during the morning rush hour on May 28, with witnesses saying ‌he was inhaling from a balloon and weaving between lanes.
Police later found Sterling sitting in the passenger seat of his crashed car holding two canisters of nitrous oxide. No other vehicles were ⁠involved and no injuries were ⁠reported.

pg:https://www.skysports.com/football/ne.desc: Raheem Sterling pleaded guilty at Basingstoke Magistrates Court in September and admitted possession of six nitrous oxide cannisters for wrongful inhalation and failing to provide a specimen
paras: Former England player Raheem Sterling has been given a suspended 12-month jail sentence for dangerous driving and possession of nitrous oxide after a crash involving a Lamborghini on the motorway.

Sterling pleaded guilty at Basingstoke Magistrates' Court in September to driving a Lamborghini Urus dangerously on the M25, the M3, the A327 and Minley Road before he crashed on May 28. The sentence is suspended for 18 months.
He has also been handed a two-year driving ban and must undertake 100 hours of unpaid community work. Sterling will have to re-take a driving test to hold a licence.

pg:https://www.npr.org/2026/11/25/nx-s1-.desc: The Politburo member is the latest senior official targeted in President Xi Jinping's long-running anti-corruption campaign, which has shown no signs of letting up in scope or depth.
paras: BANGKOK — Chinese Communist Party authorities are investigating Shanghai party secretary Chen Jining for suspected violations of party discipline, China's anti-corruption watchdog said Tuesday.
The Politburo member is the latest senior official targeted in President Xi Jinping's long-running anti-corruption campaign, which has shown no signs of letting up in scope or depth.
Chen is under investigation by the Central Commission for Discipline Inspection. The brief announcement by China's Central Commission for Discipline Inspection provided no further details.

pg:https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/1.desc: Chen is the fourth high-ranking Politburo member to be pushed out in two years.
paras: The Chinese Communist Party has launched investigations into the party’s Shanghai secretary Chen Jining for alleged “serious violations of discipline and law” – usually code for corruption.
The anticorruption watchdog, the Central Commission for Discipline Inspection, announced the probe in a brief statement on Tuesday, according to Xinhua News Agency, but did not give more details.

It comes amid widespread purges in the Political Bureau, one of the top bodies of the CCP, as the party prepares for its next congress in the second half of 2027, where President Xi Jinping is expected to clinch his fourth five-year term.

pg:https://www.theguardian.com/world/202.desc: Operation in which one hostage-taker was killed ends daylong siege in Cartagena shopping centre, where 30 people were initially held
paras: Colombian security forces have stormed a supermarket in the Caribbean city of Cartagena, ending a daylong hostage siege, with the president saying all those held had been rescued and one hostage-taker killed.
Several explosions were heard before security forces entered the building, where about 20 people were believed to be being held by armed men.
President Abelardo de la Espriella, said: “In an extraordinary joint operation between the national police and the armed forces, all the hostages were rescued.”

pg:https://www.theguardian.com/uk-news/2.desc: Mirgen Doku and Arilen Ndoci to appear before magistrates over suspected break-in at Anmer Hall in Norfolk
paras: Two men have been charged with burglary and trespass after a suspected break-in at the Prince and Princess of Wales’s country mansion.
Mirgen Doku, 34, and Arilen Ndoci, 32, both Albanian nationals, were due to appear at Norwich magistrates court on Wednesday over the incident at Anmer Hall in Norfolk on Monday evening.

Norfolk police previously said specialist resources, including police dogs, drones and the national police air service helicopter, were deployed to assist with searches in the area after they received a call at 6pm.

pg:https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/c6y.desc: Chen Jining's fall is part of the widest purge in the party's Politburo in several decades.
paras: Chen Jining, 62, is suspected of "severe violations of discipline and laws", according to a statement published on Tuesday by the party's anti-corruption body.
Chen is now the fourth member of the elite Politburo to be investigated, in the widest purge yet of the party's top executive body since the end of the Cultural Revolution.
As the party prepares to appoint fresh leaders at next year's National People's Congress, uncertainty looms over what its new command will look like - except that Xi will remain at the helm.

pg:https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2.desc: Controlled blast to proceed after multiple delays and outpouring of concern about potential health and environmental effects
paras: The US Army is set to detonate the nation’s entire stockpile of lead azide in Iowa on Wednesday morning, moving ahead after multiple delays and despite an outpouring of public concern about potential health and environmental effects.

The controlled blast is planned to dispose of 9,700lb (4,400kg) of the bomb-making chemicals stored at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant in Middletown, a small town in south-eastern Iowa that is home to about 400 people. The explosion risks releasing plumes of toxic chemicals in a 100-mile (160km) radius, but exactly where those toxins will land has changed as the weather forecast changes.
On Tuesday, the army released new maps forecasting that the projected path will move south-west of Middletown before extending into northern Missouri.

pg:https://www.theguardian.com/football/.desc: Raheem Sterling has avoided jail, receiving a 12 month sentence suspended for 18 months at Basingstoke magistrates court
paras: Raheem Sterling has avoided jail for dangerous driving while inhaling nitrous oxide, receiving a 12-month sentence suspended for 18 months at Basingstoke magistrates court on Wednesday.

The former England international was also ordered to do 100 hours of community service. His MBE and charitable and foundation work was accepted in mitigation, together with his decision to voluntarily submit to addiction treatment.
Sterling pleaded guilty in September to dangerous driving after driving his Lamborghini for more than an hour on motorways during rush hour while inhaling nitrous oxide in May.

pg:https://www.thehindu.com/sci-tech/sci.desc: Beaver Supermoon 2026 explained: what it is, why November’s moon appears larger, and when the next supermoons will occur.
paras: The full supermoon, also known as the Beaver Moon, rises behind the Chrysler Building and the Manhattan skyline as a helicopter flies past in New York City, US, November 24, 2026. | Photo Credit: REUTERS

Skywatchers were treated to a dazzling view as the Beaver Supermoon lit up the night skies on Tuesday (November 24, 2026). The November full moon, known as the Beaver Moon, appears larger and brighter than usual due to its proximity to Earth. Here is more about the celestial display and when you can watch the next supermoon

The moon revolves around the Earth in an oval-shaped path (elliptical orbit). A supermoon occurs when the moon rises near perigee (the point in its orbit closest to earth), appearing larger and brighter than usual. This year’s full moon (November 24) is known as the Beaver Supermoon because this is when beavers prepare for the winter and also the time of year to set beaver traps before the swamps and rivers froze.

pg:https://www.cbsnews.com/news/china-la.desc: China has launched the Shenzhou 24 spacecraft with three astronauts, sending the first foreign crew member to its space station.
paras: China on Wednesday launched the Shenzhou 24 spacecraft with three astronauts — two Chinese and a Pakistani — sending the first foreign crew member to its space station.

Pakistani astronaut Muhammad Zeeshan Ali, 40, is flying alongside Chinese astronauts Tang Hongbo, 51, and Wu Yi, 39, after the craft blasted off from the Jiuquan Satellite Launch Center in northwestern China on Wednesday morning. It successfully separated from a rocket and entered its predetermined orbit.
The launch marked the first joint flight involving Chinese and foreign astronauts in the history of China's manned space program.

pg:https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2.desc: Divers recover bodies after Cessna 210 went down in Gulf of Mexico on Tuesday afternoon killing all onboard
paras: Divers have found the bodies of six people killed in a small plane crash on Tuesday off the coast of Mississippi, according to the US Coast Guard.

Their bodies were in the plane’s fuselage after the Cessna 210 went down in the Gulf of Mexico between Pascagoula, Mississippi, and Horn Island, which is part of the Gulf Islands national seashore. Four adults and two boys, ages eight and 10, were onboard, a Coast Guard spokesperson, Juan Ros, said.

The air traffic control regional tower in Mobile, Alabama, reported about 3.45pm that it lost contact with the aircraft, according to the Coast Guard. Responders searched for hours and initially only found three lifejackets, a life raft and the plane’s cabin floating on the water, according to Ros.

paras: The new taxes charged on imports to America are set to hit many of country's biggest trading partners, with China, the European Union and 12 other jurisdictions.

The move comes after the White House's investigation into the trade practices of other countries in March after the US Supreme Court ruled Trump's previously announced Liberation Day tariffs were illegal.

pg:https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/1.desc: Solomon Islands will have to consult Canberra before making new security or infrastructure deals under new pact.
paras: Solomon Islands and Australia have signed a sweeping treaty affirming that the small Pacific country will allow no foreign military bases on its territory.
The deal, signed on Wednesday, is seen as a blow to the regional ambitions of China, which had been moving closer to the Solomon Islands for years.

The treaty establishes Australia as the island nation’s “primary security partner” and will see Canberra provide 740 million Australian dollars ($490m) over the next 10 years to fund free education and other programmes in Solomon Islands. Solomon Islands has a gross domestic product (GDP) of $1.75bn, according to the World Bank.

pg:https://www.npr.org/2026/11/25/g-s1-1.desc: Authorities have evacuated a 5-mile radius to prepare to dispose of thousands of pounds of lead azide. And, after a nearly two-year legal battle, Kilmar Abrego Garcia's has voluntarily left the U.S.
paras: The Army will detonate a huge explosion in Middletown, Iowa, this morning to safely dispose of thousands of pounds of lead azide that could spontaneously explode. The explosive has been used since WWI and was moved to the Iowa bunker 17 years ago. The detonation is happening after officials found that the lead azide had crystallized and become unstable. Authorities have evacuated a 5-mile radius, and those within 20 miles are advised to stay indoors to avoid exposure to toxins.

Kilmar Abrego Garcia has voluntarily left the U.S. after a nearly two-year legal battle. He is the Salvadoran immigrant who became emblematic of the challenges posed by President Trump's mass deportation campaign. Abrego Garcia was arrested in 2025 and mistakenly deported to El Salvador. He returned to the U.S. but departed for Spain yesterday. His lawyer, Simon Sandoval-Moshenberg, said that Abrego Garcia boarded a commercial flight to a destination of his choice and "left the United States a free man." Sandoval-Moshenberg described the move as "a temporary departure," saying that Abrego Garcia, whose wife and child are U.S. citizens, has options to return to the U.S.

Nvidia's newly reinstated CEO, Jensen Huang, apologized to his staff yesterday for his previous behavior, according to the New York Times. He reportedly denied that Trump pressured the board for his return, despite the president saying otherwise. Huang had stepped down following reports of affairs, including one with a woman reportedly suspected by U.S. intelligence agencies of being recruited by China's spy agency. Some members of Congress still have concerns about the national security scandal.

paras: WASHINGTON: United States President Donald Trump on Wednesday (Nov 25) fired a new tariff salvo on 14 major trading partners, including China, Japan, the European Union and Singapore, undeterred in his protectionist push by the losses his Republican Party suffered in US midterm elections.

His administration proposed new headline tariff rates of 20 per cent to 40 per cent, but said duties would be capped at lower levels agreed under trade deals that have already been concluded or remain under negotiation.

Under the main "Section 301" probe into excess industrial capacity, China would face the highest capped rate of 20 per cent, which would be added to duties of roughly 25 per cent imposed during Trump's first term.

pg:https://www.theguardian.com/tv-and-ra.desc: In this adaptation of the sci-fi franchise Michelle Yeoh and Hunter Schafer are on a quest to track down a group of replicants gone rogue. It’s a neon-filled world of beautiful doomsday visions
paras: In this adaptation of the sci-fi franchise Michelle Yeoh and Hunter Schafer are on a quest to track down a group of replicants gone rogue. It’s a neon-filled world of beautiful doomsday visions

Blade Runner has always been relevant to the age of AI, in that its starting point is that enslaved robots have rebelled. But the new version, the story’s first expansion into television, is acutely topical in an era where we’re increasingly anxious about whether what we’re seeing – or reading – is the work of machines. Fifty years on from the events of the last movie, the replicants have won: “Blade runners” are now replicants hunting down disobedient humans rather than the other way around, and the capture and storage of human memories is illegal. As humanity dies, what it remembers has become valuable contraband.

Since it is ultimately about the video fragments in our minds, Blade Runner has, from the start, presented its conception of the future as more of a mood than a story. One of the many things Blade Runner 2099 creator/writer Silka Luisa gets right is keeping that allusive wooziness, prioritising images over details and vibes over the desire to build a complete, logically functioning world. It’s important to, uh, remember that before diving in.

pg:https://www.cbc.ca/news/world/us-spai.desc: Kilmar Abrego Garcia, the Salvadoran national who fought his mistaken deportation from the U.S., arrived in Spain on Wednesday after voluntarily leaving the United States, potentially ending a defining saga of the Trump administration's immigration crackdown.
paras: Abrego Garcia was arrested in Baltimore in March 2025 and deported to an El Salvador prison despite never having been convicted of a crime in the U.S.

Other countries affected by the new tariffs include Bangladesh, ‌Cambodia, the European Union, India, Indonesia, Japan, South Korea, Malaysia, Singapore, Switzerland, Taiwan, Thailand and Vietnam.

paras: More than 490,000 Russian soldiers have died since Vladimir Putin ordered Russia's ongoing full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022, according to leaked Russian government data analyzed by CBS News partner network BBC News. Another organization's analysis of the vast dataset suggests the toll is likely closer to 700,000.

A recent hack by pro-Ukraine groups Belarusian Cyber Partisans BY and Ukraine's Silent Crow produced the data that was analyzed by the BBC and independent Russian outlet Mediazona. It included more than 11 million death records from 2021 to September 2026, according to the British broadcaster.

The data, which includes granular information on the location of deaths in Ukraine and Russian border regions, age ranges, causes of death, and employment and court rulings suggests at least 490,334 Russian soldiers have died during the war so far, according to the BBC. According to Mediazona's analysis, which the outlet said accounted for delays in death registrations, missing records and deaths occurring since the data was leaked, Russia's total military death toll has likely reached around 700,000.

pg:https://www.politico.eu/article/cop-i.desc: The chaotic conclusion of the COP31 conference is turning nations against the process.

Rifts proved so fractious at the talks in Antalya, Turkey, that governments could not seal a high-level deal for the first time since 2009. That has led ministers, negotiators and other officials to call for changes to a process that has for decades required a consensus of nearly 200 nations to move forward.

pg:https://kotaku.com/the-non-gamers-gui.desc: What even is this big game that everyone around you is suddenly talking and post about?
paras: Grand Theft Auto 6 is everywhere you look. Every news channel is talking about it. Celebrities and musicians are playing GTA 6 or posting about its release. Perhaps someone sent you this link because you kept asking them GTA 6 questions. Maybe you did a Google search, made it past the AI results and found this blog explaining what GTA 6 is to people who don’t buy or play games. Whatever the case, welcome. pg:https://www.theguardian.com/commentis.desc: Microaggressions pile up, and then they are triggering. Amid the latest row on I’m a Celebrity, we’re obliged to explain this hurt all over again, says author and journalist Natalie Morris
paras: Microaggressions pile up, and then they are triggering. Amid the latest row on I’m a Celebrity, we’re obliged to explain this hurt all over again

When I heard Mariella Frostrup call AJ Odudu “aggressive” over the weekend on I’m a Celebrity … Get Me Out of Here!, my heart sank with sick recognition. For her part, AJ’s mother has since said that watching her daughter experience this all-too-familiar dynamic was a “living hell”. I know many Black women tuning in will have felt a collective shudder of disgust and solidarity.

Of course, there is pushback. “Our addiction to offence is tearing us apart,” wrote a Telegraph pundit on Monday. But, this language is not neutral. There is a long history of Black women having their conduct and tone disproportionately scrutinised by white people. And what happened between Odudu and Frostrup is a tale as old as time. A Black woman stands up for herself and, no matter how reasonably she presents her argument, she is accused of aggression. It is an efficient tactic to flip the focus on to the behaviour of the Black woman, and it is rooted in racist stereotypes.

paras: He had been diagnosed with stage four metastatic prostate cancer in 2018, which he disclosed publicly in 2022 when Duran Duran were about to be inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame.

A statement from Duran Duran added: “Andy was there at the very beginning of our story. From the moment he arrived in Birmingham from the North East with a guitar and an unshakeable belief in what we could become, he brought an indelible fire and swagger to our music. His playing drove the songs that took us around the world, and with a dry wit that was matched only by his wonderfully unsentimental, no-nonsense outlook on life he kept us grounded and gave the band its edge through the extraordinary years that followed.”

The following month Simon Le Bon joined as frontman, by February 1981 they had released their debut single Planet Earth, and with the July release of Girls on Film – a song propelled by Taylor’s ultra-tight and rhythmic playing – they became major stars in the UK and US. Rio, their second album released in 1982, cemented their international playboy image and went Top 10 in both countries, and follow-up Seven and the Ragged Tiger topped the UK chart. Speaking to Smash Hits in 1983, Taylor described his new-found career as “a hobby gone mad”. That year Taylor also opened a wine bar called Rio, in Whitley Bay in his native Tyneside.

With their new game, Grand Theft Auto VI, they have slowed things down even more. There are still, to be sure, plenty of sequences featuring the high-octane action the series is known for. But it’s the game’s banality that seems to be sticking with players just as much. In between missions featuring gunfights, police chases and robberies, players spend just as much time on activities that are entirely mundane. In a genre – a medium, even – so committed to constant stimulation of your dopamine receptors, Grand Theft Auto VI manages to be most engaging when you’re forced to take your time.

pg:https://www.engadget.com/2325713/gran.desc: The struggle in GTA6 is both real and virtual.
paras: Devindra Hardawar for Engadget Add Engadget on Google: Google Discover Even when they were well written, every GTA story has ultimately been about solving your problems with the accumulation of wealth. But Grand Theft Auto 6 specifically focuses on the systemic issues that make any version of the American Dream — saving money, buying a home and supporting a family with a fulfilling job — incredibly difficult for people living on the margins of society. The crushing weight of capitalism is always pressing down on you, just like in the real world.

Lucia Caminos committed an ill-conceived robbery, is subsequently sent to jail and is forced to claw her way back into civilian life with little support. Jason Duval joined the Army to escape his troubled youth and ends up serving as muscle for a small-time criminal. Much like the real Bonnie and Clyde, Lucia and Jason are driven by the need to escape poverty, but it's up to you to determine if they'll share a similar end.

I only have around 12 hours of GTA 6 under my belt so far (it's estimated to take around 50 hours to beat, and hundreds of hours to fully complete), but Rockstar clearly frames why our lead characters pursue a life of crime: beyond the generational poverty and lack of upward mobility, Lucia and Jason are also trying to build enough stability to reclaim custody of their infant son.

pg:https://finance.biggo.com/news/6012b2.desc: The European Space Agency's Hera probe has delivered the first close-up look at Dimorphos since NASA's DART spacecraft struck it in 2022, finding that…
paras: Hera, which launched in October 2024 and arrived at the binary asteroid system on Nov. 4, has found that the face of Dimorphos struck by DART was compressed into an impact basin roughly the size of a sports stadium and stretching across the asteroid's full width. The 2022 collision also appears to have altered the body's overall shape and left it rotating erratically.

The findings were released alongside the first batch of close-up imagery, presented during a live broadcast on Wednesday, giving the public its first detailed look at the crash site since the Double Asteroid Redirection Test struck on Sept. 26, 2022.

DART was designed as a planetary defense experiment: a deliberate, high-speed collision to test whether humanity could nudge a threatening space rock off course. The target, Dimorphos, is a small moonlet orbiting the larger asteroid Didymos. The spacecraft hit at roughly 14,000 miles per hour (about 22,500 kilometers per hour), throwing a plume of debris into space and shortening the moonlet's orbital period around Didymos by about 33 minutes.

pg:https://www.popsci.com/science/dart-m.desc: The ESA's first detailed images of Dimorphos are here.
paras: Add Popular Science (opens in a new tab) After over four years of years of anticipation, the European Space Agency has obtained images detailing the aftermath of NASA’s head-on collision with the asteroid Dimorphos. The photos and scans from ESA’s Hera spacecraft highlight the results of the Double Asteroid Redirection Test’s (DART) intentional run-in with Didymos’ 500-foot-wide moonlet Dimorphos in 2022, revealing a stadium-sized crater, cloud of boulders, and a new, erratic orbital path.

Michel explained that while DART flattened one side of Dimorphos into a massive crater, the rest of the space rock isn’t much different. Fields of boulders largely remain where they could be seen in DART’s photos from 2022, although the event did drastically change the binary system’s surroundings.
Hera employed three instruments during its first observations—a thermal infrared imager to measure surface temperature, a 25-color multispectral imager, and a monochrome camera.

DART was sent on a proof-of-principle mission for ‌using a spacecraft to change a celestial object’s trajectory. Dimorphos, an oblong-shaped rocky object about 495 feet (151 meters) wide, orbits its companion asteroid Didymos, with ‌a diameter of 2,395 feet (730 meters), and the pair is currently about 120 ‌million miles (193.5 ⁠million km) from Earth.

They are defined as near-Earth asteroids, though neither object ⁠imperils Earth. Previous data showed how DART succeeded in changing the path of Dimorphos — demonstrating that a spacecraft could alter the trajectory of an object headed toward a collision with Earth. pg:https://www.theguardian.com/music/202.desc: Taylor was absolutely integral to the success of Duran Duran, and not merely because he was by far the most straightforwardly talented musician in the band
paras: It’s very easy indeed to paint Andy Taylor as the misfit within the world-beating five-man line-up of Duran Duran. The others were fans of glam and Chic: their avowed intention was to form a band that melded the sophisticated disco of the latter with the extravagant style and experimental art-pop of Roxy Music.

Happy enough initially to apply the hair dye and make-up that gave Duran Duran their hip post-punk New Romantic image, by the mid-80s he looked like he’d joined the wrong band entirely. In the photos of Duran Duran taken at the Sanremo pop festival in 1985, his bandmates sport the kind of baggy, spendy designer gear common to British pop stars of the era who’ve done exceptionally well for themselves. By contrast, Andy Taylor looks like he could have been parachuted in from a heavy metal band: his hair long, his ripped vest accessorised with scarves, his belt studded, his eyes hidden behind a pair of sunglasses.

Like drummer Roger Taylor, he left Duran Duran the following year: unlike Roger Taylor, he left not because he could no longer stand the pressure of being a global teen idol and fancied a quiet life, but because he’d negotiated a solo deal with a record label that would allow him to pursue his passion for hard rock, in the company of former Sex Pistols guitarist Steve Jones.

pg:https://www.thecut.com/article/can-yo.desc: For some couples, the video game has become a Rorschach test for their love lives.
paras: In the mere days since GTA VI launched on November 19, social media has been awash with opinions about the romance at the heart of the long-awaited video game. The first portion predominantly follows Jason, a ripped dude doing illicit odd jobs in the South Florida suburb of Leonida (a stone’s throw from Vice City, the game’s version of Miami). After Lucia, his girlfriend and the mother of his son, calls him from prison with unexpected news — she’s getting out early — Jason faces a choice ahead of her arrival: Does he put in the effort to make Lucia feel welcome and appreciated, such as repairing the creaky steps at home, rearranging furniture, and picking up groceries? Or does he do nothing?

GTA VI is a game of staggering scale. It’s the biggest entertainment release in history, notching $3.8 billion in sales in just one day, with an estimated 33,000 different non-playable characters one can interact with in a sprawling world. So perhaps it should come as no surprise that its influence has spread beyond the console: The game’s fictional landscape has become a Rorschach test for IRL relationships. For some, the romance between Jason and Lucia is capable of revealing the best and worst qualities of their own love lives.

Moraes posits that GTA VI provides a rare opportunity for people to see how their partners engage in a romance apart from the one they’re actually living in. “Even though it’s this very small virtual relationship, the player is still making relationship choices,” Moraes says. “Sometimes it can be hard to see, when you’re in a relationship, if it’s bad or if it’s toxic. But then you’re seeing it from an outsider’s perspective, and you can maybe be a little bit more attuned to whether your partner is treating this character right or not.”

pg:https://www.theguardian.com/sport/202.desc: The quarterback’s spectacularly messy exit from Pittsburgh could herald an overdue collapse at one of the NFL’s most famous franchises
paras: Nobody in the world, except maybe Pittsburgh Steelers owner Art Rooney II, is surprised that the franchise’s marriage of convenience with Aaron Rodgers ended in spectacular flames. Despite their own elevated idea of themselves, Pittsburgh have been one of the NFL’s messiest soap operas for a solid decade. When they linked up with the league’s messiest quarterback, it seemed certain we would get … even more mess. When they doubled down last offseason by hiring the coach with whom Rodgers had fallen out in Green Bay in the late 2010s, the mess became inevitable. We’d seen hints of the approaching drama in the season’s first 11 weeks.

But give this to the Steelers, and to Rodgers: no matter how trashy each party has been for however many years, the show they gave us on Wednesday was special – right up there with the Hindenburg’s final moments. The league’s most dramatic, selfish quarterback collided with the NFL franchise that has the most outdated and over-inflated view of itself, and the result was the greatest explosion in modern history between a team and their QB.

Rodgers, who isn’t known for his humility, has strange tendencies on his best days, and if you don’t find him a reliable narrator, you’re well within your rights. But McCarthy admitted to the “Packers” mishap during his own news conference on Wednesday, and various Steelers players had the chance to support their coach during media availabilities after practice and decided not to. “It’s all true,” one source told ESPN’s Brooke Pryor, whose story on Wednesday appeared to corroborate many of Rodgers’s claims about McCarthy.

paras: Watching Miatta Fahnbulleh, the secretary of state for energy security and net zero, forced to defend the government’s retreat from net zero (Where do people want to see Britain’s climate action plan working? On their own doorstep, 17 November) was painfully reminiscent of the way in which Colin Powell, a former US secretary of state and an honourable man, was forced to defend George W Bush’s claims justifying the disastrous Iraq war.

Fahnbulleh states that people need to see the benefits of net zero on their doorstep – meaning jobs, cost of living and warm homes. But in fact the policies of this government mark a retreat of all of these “doorstep” benefits. Andy Burnham has slashed heat pump subsidies, which means more vulnerability of homes to heating price shocks from international affairs spiking fossil gas prices; it also means fewer warm homes and jobs in the heat pump manufacturing and installation industry.

The impending rollback of the electric vehicle mandate means more costs for drivers, who will continue to pay high prices for petrol, and an ultimate collapse of jobs in the UK auto industry, which will be unable to compete with the inexorable shift to electric vehicles. And Fahnbulleh turned down the Botley West project, which would have been the UK’s biggest solar farm and would have done more for the country’s energy security (and jobs) than the contributions of Jackdaw gas or Rosebank oil (destined in any case for export).

paras: He may be a proud petrolhead with a racing licence … but superstars have been lured in before then flounced off. The BBC simply can’t afford for that to happen again

Stuart HeritageThu 26 Nov 2026 10.46 GMTLast modified on Thu 26 Nov 2026 11.46 GMTShare Prefer the Guardian on Google There is a lot riding on 2028’s Top Gear revival. Ever since The Punch That Changed Everything, the series has ostensibly remained the BBC’s landmark motoring show, even though several successive iterations have demonstrably been nothing of the sort. But hope springs eternal, and this time the BBC seems to be pinning everything it’s got on Gordon Ramsay.

And, look, let’s get the bad stuff out of the way first. At first glance this looks very much like the BBC has done another Joey. Ramsay is a huge name. Famous, wealthy, instantly recognisable and with global appeal, he has the potential to open Top Gear up to a brand new audience.

pg:https://www.cbsnews.com/news/egypt-fu.desc: A massive fire killed 31 people in Egypt after a speeding driver allegedly crashed into a fuel tanker truck.
paras: Cairo — A massive fire on an Egyptian highway killed 31 people and injured 21 others after a car slammed into a fuel tanker truck at high speed, Egypt's Public Prosecution office said Thursday.
The driver has been arrested, according to the statement. At least 27 vehicles, including cars and motorcycles, were destroyed in the fire.
The prosecutor said the suspect admitted causing the accident while driving around 70 miles per hour on a major highway in the Al-Warraq district of Giza, which is part of the Greater Cairo area.

pg:https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/c9k.desc: The carrier is looking for urgent funding, but will file for bankruptcy without a financial lifeline.
paras: The airline uses a fleet of 12 Boeing 787 aircraft on long-haul routes from a number of European airports, including London Gatwick, Rome and Oslo.
One aircraft was meant to depart London for Orlando this morning, while another was meant to arrive from Cape Town this evening.
The suspension has also affected Pakistan International Airlines, which had been leasing aircraft and crews from Norse Atlantic.

pg:https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/1.desc: Egypt has suffered another tragedy as a deadly road explosion kills 31 and injures dozens.
paras: An explosion rocked a highway in Cairo when a fuel truck overturned and caught fire, killing at least 31 people on Wednesday.
Egypt’s public prosecutor has announced an investigation into the crash, and the Ministry of Health said it will continue to monitor the situation.
But Egypt is no stranger to deadly accidents on its roads, despite spending billions of dollars on its transportation systems.

pg:https://www.npr.org/2026/11/26/g-s1-1.desc: As the fast-moving outbreak continues to spread in eastern Congo, fighting between rebels and the army is disrupting efforts to contain the spread of the disease.
paras: BUNIA, Congo — The fast-moving Ebola outbreak in eastern Congo has topped 12,000 confirmed cases, government data showed Thursday, as fighting between rebels and the army disrupts efforts to contain the spread of the disease.

It is the fastest-growing Ebola outbreak in history and nearly half the 12,021 people confirmed to have the virus have died, according to data from Congo's Ministry of Health. It is also the deadliest of Congo's 17 outbreaks and is on track to surpass the death toll from the West African outbreak that killed 11,000 people between 2014 and 2016.

The outbreak declared in May is caused by the rare Bundibugyo virus, for which there is no approved vaccine or treatment. Response teams are battling armed conflict, poor roads and violence from residents fueled by mistrust and misinformation.

paras: Heavy rain, winds, flooding and high tides are hitting the eastern and western US, snarling travel and leading to the cancellations of at least two commercial Thanksgiving parades.
On the East Coast, authorities in Philadelphia ordered the city’s Thanksgiving Day parade in Philadelphia off the streets and will be featured as an “alternative TV event”.
In New York, the Macy’s parade of vast, inflatable characters was postponed to Saturday. One estimate put the cost of re-inflating the balloons with helium at $1.7m.

pg:https://www.cbc.ca/news/health/ebola-.desc: The number of confirmed Ebola cases in Democratic Republic of Congo now exceeds 12,000, government data showed on Thursday, as responders continue to struggle to bring the second-largest outbreak on record under control.
paras: The outbreak, caused by the rare Bundibugyo species of the Ebola virus, officially began in mid-May in the northeastern province Ituri, and has since spread to eight of the country's 26 provinces.
There are no approved treatments or vaccines for this strain of Ebola, complicating efforts to combat the disease.
Delayed detection, armed conflicts in the region and strained health services have also led to rapid spread, with mistrust and misinformation keeping some residents from seeking medical care.

pg:https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/1.desc: The judge said the FCC chair has taken US President Donald Trump's rhetoric ‌‌as his 'marching orders'.
paras: A United States judge has barred the Federal Communications Commission (FCC) from putting the licences of eight Walt Disney-owned ABC TV stations up for early review, a blow ⁠⁠to President Donald Trump’s efforts to rein in US media companies.

US District Judge Loren AliKhan, in Washington, DC, granted Disney’s request for a preliminary injunction on Wednesday. The injunction barred the FCC from holding a hearing on the licences, a step that could have led to their revocation and forced the stations off ⁠⁠the air.

AliKhan, who was nominated by former President Joe Biden, said ABC had detailed “a campaign of retaliation against them in response to their exercise of their First Amendment rights,” which on its own is an ‘irreparable injury’”.

paras: Hope the exposure to lead has been minimal. I guess they couldn’t move the bomb chemicals to a more isolated area?

The plan for the detonation set off concerns about potential health and environmental impacts from lead dust, and frustration over a lack of information.

pg:https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/cmn.desc: Veruschka was a model and artist who became one of one of the first global fashion stars in the 1960s.
paras: She became known as the striking subject of fantastical photoshoots that helped expand the boundaries of fashion and beauty in the 60s and 70s, appearing on the cover of American Vogue 13 times.
Vogue's obituary described her as "the shape-shifting supermodel who defined an era", explaining: "One of the original supermodels, Veruschka was also among fashion's great performance artists."
She also made memorable appearances in classic swinging 60s film Blow Up and 2006 James Bond movie Casino Royale.

pg:https://www.dw.com/en/egypt-at-least-.desc: The accident occurred on the packed Ring Road in Giza near Cairo. Dozens of ambulances responded to the crash, and Egyptian health authorities say the death toll could rise.
paras: The fuel tanker crash ignited a massive blaze on Ring Road in Giza's Waraq district. The Ring Road encircles the greater Cairo metropolitan area.

Egyptian Health Minister Khaled Abdel Ghaffar said the injured were transported to nearby hospitals and added that the death toll could rise further. He said 39 ambulances are responding to the accident.
A massive fire broke out after the accident, with rescue workers pulling people from their vehicles. A large crowd gathered in the densely populated Waraq neighborhood amid the rescue efforts.

pg:https://english.aawsat.com/varieties/.desc: Dimorphos, the small asteroid struck by NASA's DART spacecraft in 2022 in the first test of a planetary defense system, was left with one side flattened with a stadium-sized crater and is tumbling in space, as shown by images taken by the European Space Agency's Hera spacecraft released on Wednesday.
paras: Dimorphos, the small asteroid struck by NASA's DART spacecraft in 2022 in the first test of a planetary defense system, was left with one side flattened with a stadium-sized crater and is tumbling in space, as shown by images taken by the European Space Agency's Hera spacecraft released on Wednesday.

DART was sent on a proof-of-principle mission for using a spacecraft to change a celestial object's trajectory. Dimorphos, an oblong-shaped rocky object about 495 feet (151 meters) wide, orbits its companion asteroid Didymos, with a diameter of 2,395 feet (730 meters), and the pair is currently about 120 million miles (193.5 million km) from Earth.

They are defined ⁠as near-Earth asteroids, ⁠though neither object imperils Earth. Previous data showed how DART succeeded in changing the path of Dimorphos — demonstrating that a spacecraft could alter the trajectory of an object headed toward a collision with Earth. Hera is now getting a close-up look at how DART physically changed Dimorphos.

pg:https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/c.desc: Black smoke could be seen across Bangkok's skyline after the blast, as officials urged residents to leave the area.
paras: Seven people have been injured - four of them critically - after an explosion at an oil refinery in Bangkok, local government officials have said.

pg:https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2.desc: The army blows up US stockpile of lead azide, a chemical used for explosives, to avoid uncontrollable explosion
paras: The US army blew up the nation’s entire stockpile of lead azide, a chemical used to make explosives, saying the first checks show Wednesday’s controlled detonation in Iowa didn’t spread toxic dust to nearby homes and farms.

Earthen barriers were put up and foam and water were poured onto a pair of bunkers holding the 5 tons (4,500kg) of lead azide, and officials said those measures appear to have absorbed much of the blast.

The US Environmental Protection Agency air monitors were detecting no lead in the air around the Iowa army ammunition plant in Middletown, and an alert sent to cellphones late Wednesday afternoon said it was safe to resume normal activities. Fema also issued an all clear around the plant, the US army reported.

pg:https://www.thehindu.com/news/interna.desc: U.K. net migration drops to 77,000 — the lowest since 1997 — with Indians as the largest immigrant and emigrant group entering for study and work.
paras: File picture of the U.K. Border control in Terminal 2 at Heathrow Airport in London, Britain. The net migration figure, which represents the number of people arriving in the U.K. minus those emigrating, fell dramatically from 2,04,000 for the year ending June 2025 and from a record high of 9,00,000 in the year ending June 2023. | Photo Credit: Reuters

Net migration to the U.K. has fallen to 77,000, its lowest levels since 1997, excluding the pandemic, as per official U.K. government figures released on Thursday (November 26, 2026). Indians constituted the largest foreign nationality group immigrating and emigrating longterm to and from the U.K.

The net migration figure, which represents the number of people arriving in the U.K. minus those emigrating, fell dramatically from 2,04,000 for the year ending June 2025 and from a record high of 906,000 in the year ending June 2023. The news is likely to a shot in the arm for the governing Labour Party, as migration has become a political lighting-rod in recent years.

pg:https://www.theguardian.com/film/2026.desc: Actor who had played fraudster Elizabeth Holmes in TV drama The Dropout reveals how she was drafted in to the hit documentary ‘at the last minute’
paras: Amanda Seyfried says that the script and footage of You Can See Everything was kept secret even from her until the last possible moment, and that despite being asked not to reveal her involvement in the project she “told a lot of people”.

Seyfried was speaking on the Jimmy Fallon Show on Tuesday, after the film’s extraordinary commercial success in North America, where it is already the third most successful documentary in box office history. Having already played You Can See Everything’s central figure, Theranos fraudster Elizabeth Holmes, in the dramatised TV series The Dropout, Seyfried was called in by directors Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim to stand in for Holmes after the latter started her prison term in 2023.

Seyfried said that, after being introduced by fellow actor Emma Stone, Fielder “just reached out and said, ‘Hey, I’d love to, like, pick your brain about, you know, your experience playing Elizabeth Holmes in The Dropout … We talked for like an hour on FaceTime about Elizabeth Holmes, and he told me that he had lived with her for a month before she went to prison.”

pg:https://www.theguardian.com/uk-news/2.desc: Woman watches her sobbing husband speak about ‘the pain I’ve caused’, as nine men accused of roles in her abuse
paras: A man who drugged and raped his wife, and invited other men into the family home to assault her, sobbed in court as he told a jury he felt “guilt and shame” over “the pain I’ve caused”.

The man, who cannot be named to protect the anonymity of his victim, looked gaunt and red-faced as he gave evidence in a trial of nine other men who are alleged to have raped or sexually assaulted the woman, or encouraged the abuse online.

He held his head in his hands at times, sighed heavily, and fought back tears as the prosecutor Louise Oakley KC read out a list of the 62 charges he had pleaded guilty to, all of which relate to his wife of four decades.

Corum extended his breakout season with another impressive outing on his 26th birthday, scoring a TD in his seventh consecutive game while the Rams (7-4) got stellar efforts from their rushing attack and a stout defense to stay firmly in the NFC playoff race.

The Rams won behind Corum, whose 32 carries were the most in the NFL this season and the most by any Rams running back in coach Sean McVay’s 10-year career. Corum had 25 carries for 161 yards in the second-half alone while Los Angeles stayed in control.

paras: A Paris court has upheld an order for French actor Gerard Depardieu to stand trial on charges of raping an actress at his Paris home in 2018, his lawyer and judicial sources say.
The Paris Court of Appeal ruled on Thursday that Depardieu should face trial over allegations of rape and sexual assault against Charlotte Arnould on August 7, 2018.

Defence lawyer Delphine Meillet told The Associated Press news agency that the 77-year-old actor would face trial on one rape charge after the court dismissed allegations relating to a second incident six days later.

pg:https://www.theguardian.com/film/2026.desc: Arnould first accused Depardieu ⁠in 2018, saying assaults occurred at his Paris home on two separate occasions when ⁠she was in her early 20s
paras: Gérard Depardieu has been ordered to stand trial on a charge of raping a female actor at his Paris home in 2018, after an appeals ⁠court rejected his attempt to avoid having the case tried.

The film star, 77, had appealed last year against an investigating magistrate’s ruling that he should stand criminal trial on charges of raping and sexually assaulting Charlotte Arnould on two occasions, but judges said on Thursday proceedings should go ahead.

The court said the star would be tried for allegedly raping Arnould on 7 August 2018, but dismissed a second allegation of rape said to have occurred the following week, on 13 August. Depardieu, one of the best-known names in French cinema, has denied wrongdoing.

pg:https://www.theguardian.com/business/.desc: Former Bank of Spain governor chosen to succeed Christine Lagarde after winning support of EU’s biggest countries
paras: Spain’s Pablo Hernández de Cos has been chosen as the next president of the European Central Bank, to succeed Christine Lagarde, after winning support from the EU’s biggest countries.
The economist and monetary policymaker will become the first Spaniard to lead the ECB, defeating his rival candidate Klaas Knot, the former head of the Dutch central bank.

EU diplomats agreed two other appointments to the ECB’s executive board on Thursday: France’s Laurence Boone and Germany’s Markus Brunnermeier. The trio of appointments was a package deal, after France and Germany converged on choosing Hernández de Cos, who is expected to keep the ECB on the same path.

Altria also said it was in discussions with a third party about its possible acquisition of part of Imperial Brands’ business, suggesting the company could be broken up.

pg:https://www.nbcconnecticut.com/news/l.desc: Two professors used computer modeling to find the best parking spot the fastest.
paras: Black Friday has been described as the busiest day for U.S. in-store holiday shopping traffic.

paras: Donald Trump has alleged without evidence that economic figures published by the US federal government before this month’s midterm elections were “fake” and demanded an investigation after voters roundly rejected his Republican party.

pg:https://www.theguardian.com/media/202.desc: John Mann says he is conducting review after hearing ‘disturbing’ accounts of discrimination from Jewish staff
paras: The government’s independent adviser on antisemitism has said he is launching an investigation into the BBC after hearing “disturbing” accounts from Jewish staff of discrimination against them.

His decision to investigate the BBC comes after a recent attempt to reassure Jewish staff that discrimination against them would not be tolerated. A former producer had said she had faced antisemitism while employed at the corporation.

paras: On the eve of Thanksgiving at the NFL halftime show, U2 performed the Dolly Parton and Bono duet, “Torn,” as the country great’s image was projected on screens surrounding the stage.

It was a poignant moment during the show, as the song was the final vocal recording of Parton’s seven-decade career. The track appears on U2’s recently debuted album, Carnaval de Luz. While Parton, who shares writing credits for the song with the band and Snow Patrol’s Johnny McDaid, originally wrote “Torn” around a story of a woman trying to choose between two men, Bono and McDaid rewrote the lyrics around a mother watching her family divided. “You name the location,” Bono told Rolling Stone for U2’s recent cover story, “but everyone knows what it is.… People say in the U.S. now, people are scared to go into Thanksgiving.”

U2’s halftime show during the NFL’s first Thanksgiving Eve game between the Green Bay Packers and Los Angeles Rams aired on Netflix. The streamer has been organizing special halftime performances since it began airing select NFL games a few years ago. Beyoncé performed at Netflix’s first NFL game on Christmas Day 2024, while Snoop Dogg took the stage last year.

pg:https://www.gsmarena.com/amazon_us_bl.desc: Black Friday is this Friday, meaning that the 7 days of sales are nearly over. Here are the biggest discounts on smartphones that we found.

pg:https://www.newsweek.com/donald-trump.desc: The president's remarks on his conversation with Putin came after he met Wednesday with NATO Secretary-General Mark Rutte.
paras: Trump's Thanksgiving morning comments on Truth Social came after he hosted NATO Secretary-General Mark Rutte at his Mar-a-Lago estate in Florida on Wednesday evening and as his son-in-law and special envoy, Jared Kushner, drew backlash for praising Putin and suggesting the Russian leader had demonstrated restraint in Ukraine.

Trump repeatedly promised during his 2024 presidential campaign that he would end the war between Russia and Ukraine within 24 hours. The president subsequently characterized the promise as an exaggeration after this did not materialize.

Nearly two years into Trump's second term, Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine continues, despite multiple rounds of U.S.-brokered negotiations. European leaders have also voiced concerns about Moscow's ambitions beyond Ukraine and the implications of any peace agreement for the continent's broader security.

pg:https://abcnews.com/Entertainment/wir.desc: French actor Gérard Depardieu has been ordered to stand trial on charges of raping and sexually assaulting a young actress at his Paris home in 2018
paras: SharePARIS -- PARIS (AP) — Gérard Depardieu, for decades one of France’s most celebrated actors, has been ordered to stand trial on charges of raping and sexually assaulting a young actress, authorities said Thursday, less than two weeks after the cinema star abandoned his appeal of a sexual assault conviction in a separate case.
Actress Charlotte Arnould was 22 when she accused Depardieu in 2018 of raping her at his Paris home.

Eight years later, the Paris Court of Appeal ruled that the actor should face trial over allegations of rape and sexual assault on Aug. 7, 2018, while dismissing allegations relating to a second incident six days later.

pg:https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/1.desc: Paris court of appeal dismisses allegations relating to a second incident involving actress Charlotte Arnould.
paras: A Paris court has upheld an order for French actor Gerard Depardieu to stand trial on charges of raping an actress at his Paris home in 2018, his lawyer and judicial sources say.
The Paris Court of Appeal ruled on Thursday that Depardieu should face trial over allegations of rape and sexual assault against Charlotte Arnould on August 7, 2018.

Defence lawyer Delphine Meillet told The Associated Press news agency that the 77-year-old actor would face trial on one rape charge after the court dismissed allegations relating to a second incident six days later.

pg:https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/ckp.desc: One gunman was killed after what the country's president described as a robbery of a cash-laden armoured car gone wrong.
paras: Gunmen had stormed into the building at 08:00 local time (13:00 GMT) on Tuesday after what Colombian President Abelardo de la Espriella described as a failed attempt at robbing an armoured car carrying money.

With the situation becoming ever more intense as the day progressed, de la Espriella gave the green light for special forces and police to launch a daring operation to free the hostages, killing one gunman.
Residents living near the supermarket reported hearing explosions as the security forces moved into the building.

paras: Donald Trump says he would like Vladimir Putin "pull back all military aggression" in Europe.

Link copied US President Donald Trump says he would like to see Russian President Vladimir Putin "pull back all military aggression against territories throughout Europe" and end the war in Ukraine faster.
Mr Trump has frequently urged a negotiated end to the war in Ukraine, but on Thursday, US time, he used broader language about "territories throughout Europe" without specifying what that meant.
